newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine wheat rain pleases exporters.
newsitem.headline: Argentine wheat rain pleases exporters.

text.p: Rain fell throughout most of Argentina's wheat belt after a long stretch of clear skies Friday, and was welcomed by traders as timely for replenishing dryer soils in northern croplands.
"It will be very good for Cordoba and Santa Fe, where it really had not rained very much," a trader said. "In some areas of the north of Buenos Aires they also needed rain so it will be excellent."
He added that the rain would do no harm in the south of Buenos Aires province, where heavy early season falls left fields waterlogged and slowed sowing.
"Sowing is pretty much over now," he said.
But he stressed falls have been light so far, with probably no more than 0.4 inches (10 mm) in most areas.
Argentina's National Meteorological Service said that a cold front had swept up from Patagonia, and would bring rain Friday to all wheat areas except for western Buenos Aires.
It forecast dryer weather for Saturday, but said showers and storms should continue in northern Santa Fe.
The government's Agriculture Secretariat said in its weekly report to August 8 Thursday that the wheat in parts of Cordoba was in bad shape and stressed due by lack of water.
But it said that wheat elsewhere was in good condition. Cordoba only accounts for about a tenth of Argentina's total wheat area.
